record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Develop the mathematical theory of conduction in quasi-crystals, including proving charge-density-wave generation at low temperature for interacting fermions in one-dimensional quasi-periodic settings and extending the resulting bridge to higher-dimensional models.

evidence.quote: Develop the mathematical theory of conduction in quasi-crystals. In one dimension it is believed that fermions develop a Charge Density Wave instability at small temperature with period equal to the inverse of the density. An interesting goal is to prove the generation of such CDW in a system of interacting Fermions... It would be nice to extend this bridge to other models, in particular in greater dimensions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional system of interacting spinless fermions on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}$ subject to a quasi-periodic external potential. Let the Hamiltonian be
$$H = -\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}}\bigl(c^{\dagger}_{x+1}c_{x}+c^{\dagger}_{x}c_{x+1}\bigr) + \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}} v(\omega x + \theta)\, c^{\dagger}_{x}c_{x} + U\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}} \bigl(c^{\dagger}_{x}c_{x}-\rho\bigr)\bigl(c^{\dagger}_{x+1}c_{x+1}-\rho\bigr),$$
where $c^{\dagger}_x, c_x$ are fermionic creation/annihilation operators, $v:\mathbb{T}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a smooth $2\pi$-periodic potential, $\omega/2\pi$ is an irrational frequency satisfying a Diophantine condition, $\theta\in\mathbb{T}$ is a phase, $U\in\mathbb{R}$ is a coupling constant, and $\rho\in(0,1)$ is the average particle density fixed by a chemical potential $\mu$.

Let $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\beta}$ denote the Gibbs state of $H$ at inverse temperature $\beta$, and let $n_x = c^{\dagger}_x c_x$. 

(a) Prove that for $|U|$ sufficiently small and $\beta$ sufficiently large (low temperature), the connected density-density correlation function develops a charge-density-wave (CDW) component with wavevector $2\pi\rho$ in the sense that
$$\langle n_x n_y\rangle_{\beta}^{c} \sim A(\beta)\cos\bigl(2\pi\rho(x-y)+\varphi\bigr) f(x-y)$$
for some non-vanishing amplitude $A(\beta)$ and slowly decaying envelope $f$, exhibiting CDW order with period equal to $\rho^{-1}$.

(b) Extend the rigorous construction of the Gibbs state and the proof of CDW generation to analogous models of interacting fermions on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d\ge 2$ in a quasi-periodic background.
artifact.status_search_result: Rigorous results exist for one-dimensional interacting fermions with strong quasi-periodic disorder, including exponential decay of correlations and vanishing Drude weight at zero temperature (Mastropietro and collaborators). However, a complete rigorous proof of charge-density-wave generation with period equal to the inverse density for interacting fermions in quasi-periodic settings, and its extension to higher dimensions, does not appear to be established in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Vanishing of Drude Weight in Interacting Fermions on Z^d with Quasi-Periodic Disorder
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous proof at zero temperature of exponential decay of correlations and vanishing of Drude weight in the strong disorder regime, combining Ward Identities, RG and KAM.
status_evidence.claim: Partial rigorous results exist for interacting fermions with quasi-periodic disorder, but full CDW generation results and higher-dimensional extensions remain open.

status_evidence.title: Ground state of one-dimensional fermion-phonon systems
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous studies of fermion models with CDW order are relatively scarce; proofs exist in specific settings but a general framework is lacking.
status_evidence.claim: General rigorous CDW results for interacting fermions in quasi-periodic potentials remain an open program.
